newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL small-caps leap ahead, blue chips close lower.
newsitem.headline: KL small-caps leap ahead, blue chips close lower.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips ended weaker, continuing to take a backseat to small-capitalisation counters, which looked set to challenge the 620 level.

Even news that a long-awaited July trade figure was below the market's worst expectations of 1 billion ringgit failed to inspire blue chip buyers. Malaysia recorded a trade gap of 624.5 million ringgit for July versus a June surplus.
The Composite Index ended down 4.09 points to 1,126.51, after barely opening firmer. The Second Board continued to sizzle, rising to a new intraday high of 619.28.
By day's end, the small-capitalisation Second Board index had retraced some gains to end up 1.35 points to 608.48.

The trade data was "not totally a surprise," said one analyst with a local firm. "What was actually announced was a mixed bag. It's positive in the sense it's lower than expected, but it's still a deficit."

While speculation of projects, deals and restructurings continue to pull retailers into the Second Board, the main boarders were weighed down by concerns about the trade number, as well as possible interest rate hikes in the U.S. The Federal Reserve's policy making arm meets on Tuesday.
